To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antibody response to a peptide of the BIV transmembrane protein is a sensitive and specific assay that may be used for identifying cattle infected with BIV in the absence of a serological response to the major envelope glycoprotein.
the antibody response to BIV peptides is useful in identifying cattle experimentally infected by BIV and that this antibody response can be detected as early as 4 weeks after infection.

(a) the antibody response to the BIV transmembrane protein is a sensitive marker of BIV infection; (b) the antibody response is not affected by coinfection with bovine herpesvirus-1; and (c) the antibody response can be used to monitor the course of BIV infection.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BIV infection of cattle is associated with the production of antibodies to a region of the transmembraneglycoprotein of the virus.

the antibody responses of cattle infected with BIV(112) to peptides of the virus transmembrane protein are similar to those of cattle infected with other viruses and that these responses can be detected by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay using peptides of the virus.

the antibody response to BIV peptides in experimentally infected cattle is similar to the antibody response to other lentiviruse peptides and that the antibody response is similar for all BIV isolates tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antibody response in cattle infected with BIV is similar in many respects to that seen in cattle infected with bovid herpesvirus 4 (bovine herpesvirus 2), a herpesvirus that causes infectious bovine rhinotracheitis, and in cattle infected with bluetongue virus, a nonenveloped virus that causes bluetongue.

this assay is useful for the detection of BIV in cattle and that the antibody response to this peptide may be useful for identifying cattle that are at risk for the development of persistent BIV infection.
we have shown that the BIV transmembrane glyco-protein is immunodominant in infected cattle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BIV transmembrane glycopeptide assay is a specific and reliable assay for BIV infection and can be used in field situations to identify BIV infection.
the antibody response to BIV can be detected early after infection, is long-lived, is specific for BIV and is not affected by the presence of other common bovine viruses.
we have a new assay for BIV infection.
